paras: Kentropyx vanzoi, also known commonly as Gallagher's kentropyx and o calanguinho-listrado in Brazilian Portuguese, is a species of lizard in the family Teiidae. The species is native to central South America.
The specific name, vanzoi, is in honor of Brazilian herpetologist Paulo Vanzolini.
K. vanzoi is found in Bolivia (Santa Cruz Department) and Brazil (Mato Grosso state).
The preferred natural habitat of K. vanzoi is savanna, at altitudes below 650 m (2,130 ft).
K. vanzoi may attain a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 6.5 cm (2.6 in). Males are greener than females, an example of sexual dimorphism.
K. vanzoi preys upon arthropods, predominately orthopterans, spiders, and termites.
K. vanzoi is oviparous. Average clutch size is three eggs.
